title: Update IR V4 types to match latest finos/morphir spec
description:
The Classic ↔ V4 converter cannot be fully implemented until we update our IR V4 type definitions to match the most recent specification from finos/morphir.

## Background
The steel thread migrate command currently only supports same-format passthrough (V4→V4, Classic→Classic). Cross-format conversion is blocked because our IR V4 types are incomplete - they use `serde_json::Value` placeholders instead of typed expressions.

## References
- V4 Spec: https://github.com/finos/morphir/blob/main/docs/spec/ir/schemas/v4/
- What's New in V4: https://github.com/finos/morphir/blob/main/docs/spec/ir/schemas/v4/whats-new.md
- Complete Example: https://github.com/finos/morphir/blob/main/docs/spec/ir/schemas/v4/complete-example.json

## Current State (What Works)
- Distribution structure (Library/Specs/Application) - matches spec
- FormatVersion (string "4.0.0" or int 4)
- Wrapper object serialization in v4.rs
- TypeAttributes/ValueAttributes with source, constraints, extensions
- Core Type enum (7 variants) - Variable, Reference, Tuple, Record, ExtensibleRecord, Function, Unit
- Core Value enum (18+ variants) including V4-only Hole, Native, External
- Literal types with IntegerLiteral (alias WholeNumberLiteral)
- JSON-level converter works for Classic ↔ V4

## Tasks (Priority Order)

### Phase 1: Serde for Type<A>
- [ ] Implement Serialize for Type<A> with V4 wrapper object format
- [ ] Implement Deserialize for Type<A> with V4 format + shorthand support
- [ ] Add tests with sample V4 type expressions
- Files: `crates/morphir-core/src/ir/type_expr.rs`, add `serde_v4.rs`

### Phase 2: Serde for Value<TA,VA>
- [ ] Implement Serialize for Value<TA,VA> with V4 wrapper object format
- [ ] Implement Deserialize for Value<TA,VA> with V4 format
- [ ] Add tests with sample V4 value expressions
- Files: `crates/morphir-core/src/ir/value_expr.rs`

### Phase 3: Replace serde_json::Value placeholders
- [ ] Replace in TypeSpecification.type_expr
- [ ] Replace in ConstructorArgSpec.arg_type
- [ ] Replace in ValueSpecification.inputs/output
- [ ] Replace in TypeDefinition.type_expr
- [ ] Replace in ConstructorArg.arg_type
- [ ] Replace in ValueDefinition.output_type
- [ ] Replace in InputTypeEntry.input_type
- [ ] Replace in ValueBody::ExpressionBody.body
- [ ] Replace in ValueAttributes.inferred_type
- File: `crates/morphir-core/src/ir/v4.rs`

### Phase 4: Add IncompleteTypeDefinition
- [ ] Add IncompleteTypeDefinition variant to TypeDefinition enum
- [ ] Include incompleteness reason (similar to HoleReason)
- [ ] Add serialization support
- Files: `crates/morphir-core/src/ir/type_def.rs`, `v4.rs`

### Phase 5: Integration Tests
- [ ] Test with real V4 IR files from finos/morphir examples
- [ ] Test round-trip conversion: V4 JSON → typed IR → V4 JSON
- [ ] Test Classic → V4 conversion produces valid V4 JSON
- [ ] Add fixtures to integration-tests/fixtures/steel-thread/

## V4 Format Details

### Wrapper Object Format
```json
{"Variable": {"name": "a"}}
{"Reference": {"fqname": "morphir/sdk:list#map", "args": [...]}}
{"Tuple": {"elements": [...]}}
{"Record": {"field-name": type, ...}}
```

### Compact Shorthand (for deserialization)
- Type variable as bare string: `"a"` instead of `{"Variable": {"name": "a"}}`
- Simple reference as FQName: `"morphir/sdk:basics#int"` 
- Reference with args: `{"Reference": ["morphir/sdk:list#list", "a"]}`

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] Type<A> and Value<TA,VA> implement Serialize + Deserialize
- [ ] All serde_json::Value placeholders replaced with typed expressions
- [ ] Round-trip V4 JSON works (deserialize → serialize = same structure)
- [ ] Classic → V4 converter produces valid typed V4 IR
- [ ] Integration tests pass with real Morphir IR files

## Blocks
- Steel thread P0 completion (cross-format migration)
- morphir-rust-steel-thread
close_reason: PR #63 merged with V4 IR types update and comprehensive test coverage

title: Steel Thread: Implement migrate command using extension architecture
description:
Build a working end-to-end slice of functionality using the migrate command as a proof-of-concept for the WASM extension architecture.

## Goal
Demonstrate the extension architecture with a real, working command: `morphir migrate` that transforms Morphir IR from v3 to v4 using a WASM extension.

## Why Migrate Command?
- **Design-time operation**: IR → IR transform (backend pattern)
- **Self-contained**: No runtime execution, no complex state
- **Real-world use case**: Actual production requirement
- **Tests full stack**: Extension loading, envelope protocol, DirectRuntime, WASM execution

## Architecture Flow
```
CLI --> DirectRuntime --> ExtismRuntime --> migrate.wasm
        (morphir-ext)     (morphir-ext)     (extension)
```

## Implementation Steps

### 1. Minimal ExtismRuntime (morphir-rust-ext1)
- [ ] Create morphir-ext/src/extism_runtime.rs
- [ ] Implement ExtismRuntime struct
- [ ] Implement call_envelope() method only
- [ ] Load WASM via Extism Manifest
- [ ] Basic error handling (map Extism errors)
- [ ] Skip TEA helpers initially

### 2. Minimal DirectRuntime (morphir-rust-direct1)
- [ ] Create morphir-ext/src/direct.rs
- [ ] Implement DirectRuntime wrapping ExtismRuntime
- [ ] Simple API: execute(func_name, input_envelope) -> output_envelope
- [ ] No actor infrastructure
- [ ] No state management initially

### 3. Minimal Host Functions (morphir-rust-std1)
- [ ] Create morphir-ext/src/host_functions.rs
- [ ] Implement log() function only (for debugging)
- [ ] Register with Extism
- [ ] Skip HTTP, workspace, IR helpers for now

### 4. Migrate Extension (WASM module)
- [ ] Create crates/morphir-migrate-extension
- [ ] Implement backend-generate interface
- [ ] Input: Envelope with IR v3 JSON
- [ ] Output: Envelope with IR v4 JSON
- [ ] Use wit-bindgen or core WASM
- [ ] Compile to WASM (wasm32-unknown-unknown)

### 5. CLI Integration
- [ ] Update morphir CLI to support extension-based migrate
- [ ] Load migrate.wasm using DirectRuntime
- [ ] Read input IR file
- [ ] Call extension with IR envelope
- [ ] Write output IR file
- [ ] Add --extension-path flag for WASM path

### 6. Testing
- [ ] Unit tests for ExtismRuntime
- [ ] Unit tests for DirectRuntime
- [ ] Integration test: Load real WASM module
- [ ] E2E test: morphir migrate with sample IR
- [ ] Test error handling (bad WASM, invalid IR, etc.)

## Success Criteria
- [ ] `morphir migrate input.json output.json` works end-to-end
- [ ] Extension loaded via ExtismRuntime
- [ ] Envelope protocol used throughout
- [ ] No daemon required (DirectRuntime only)
- [ ] Extension never sees Extism types
- [ ] Clean error messages
- [ ] Documentation of the flow

## Out of Scope (for now)
- Full TEA runtime (init/update/subscriptions)
- DaemonClient (remote execution)
- Full host function library
- Complex extensions
- Actor-based execution

## After Steel Thread
Once working, expand to:
- Full TEA runtime support
- DaemonClient implementation
- Complete host function library
- More extensions (frontends, backends)

## References
- docs/contributors/design/extensions/actor-based/12-wasm-extension-architecture-session.md
- morphir-ext/src/runtime.rs (ExtensionRuntime trait)

## Related Issues
- Part of WASM extension architecture (see morphir-rust-kw8)
- Simplifies: morphir-rust-ext1, morphir-rust-direct1, morphir-rust-std1

title: Add correlated observability and troubleshooting support
description: Define and implement local structured logging, operation and launch correlation, acquisition and launch spans, Desktop crash capture, safe retention, redaction, log discovery commands, and inspectable diagnostic bundles across morphir-cli and Morphir Desktop. design: Use versioned JSON Lines events and per-process session files beneath MORPHIR_HOME/logs. Keep console progress distinct from logs. Pass parent operation and launch IDs to Desktop. Record stable event names and error codes for resolve, fetch, verify, extract, probe, activate, rollback, spawn, ready, exit, and crash. Enable bounded local logs by default. No telemetry leaves the machine unless the user explicitly configures an exporter or submits an inspectable sanitized bundle. The first bundle contains sanitized correlated events, a system summary with normalized MORPHIR_HOME, a manifest with per-entry SHA-256 and explicit exclusions; it never reads project/config/secret content or uploads data. Morphir UI DCO commits e4f156e, 39dd400, and 78c673f add correlated Desktop JSONL, local Crashpad capture with upload disabled, failure events, active-safe 14-day/100 MiB log retention, and expired recognized minidump cleanup. title: Make YAML the primary migrate output format
description: Specify and implement YAML as a native persisted serialization of the concrete Morphir IR, with v4 as the primary target and v3 compatibility where the concrete model permits it. YAML is an equal IR storage format, not a frontend language, generated projection, or documentation view. The migrate command should default v3-to-v4 output to YAML, infer single-file encoding from the destination extension, support document-tree output, and convert stored IR bidirectionally between JSON and YAML. Update v4 so JSON Schema is clearly a bootstrap definition mechanism rather than a restriction of IR storage to JSON.
acceptance_criteria:
EARS acceptance requirements:
AC-01 ubiquitous: The IR codec system shall provide an explicit YAML representation for every valid concrete v3 and v4 IR node.
AC-02 event-driven: When the YAML decoder reads an explicit or preferred readable form, it shall normalize that form into exactly one versioned semantic IR value.
AC-03 event-driven: When the YAML encoder writes an IR value, it shall emit the specified deterministic readable form where one exists and the explicit structural form otherwise.
AC-04 event-driven: When JSON is converted to YAML to JSON without a version transform, the result shall be semantically equal to the original IR.
AC-05 event-driven: When YAML is converted to JSON to YAML without a version transform, the result shall be semantically equal to the original IR.
AC-06 ubiquitous: The codec system shall retain JSON input and output support for every previously supported IR version.
AC-07 unwanted: If YAML contains ambiguous shorthand, duplicate keys, unsupported tags, unsafe aliases, lossy numbers, or invalid coercions, then the decoder shall reject it with a located diagnostic.
AC-08 event-driven: When v3 is migrated to v4 without a selected format or recognized output extension, the command shall emit canonical YAML.
AC-09 event-driven: When resolving single-file output, the command shall apply explicit output format, recognized extension, then YAML default.
AC-10 unwanted: If output format conflicts with a recognized extension, then the command shall diagnose the conflict and shall not publish.
AC-11 event-driven: When resolving single-file input, the command shall apply explicit input format, recognized extension, then bounded JSON-first detection.
AC-12 event-driven: When --json is used without an output path, the command shall write migrated JSON IR to stdout.
AC-13 event-driven: When --json is used with an output path, the command shall write the artifact and emit JSON status and diagnostics to stdout.
AC-14 event-driven: When writing a YAML document tree, the command shall use manifest.yaml, module.yaml, *.type.yaml, and *.value.yaml.
AC-15 ubiquitous: A generated document tree shall use one serialization profile.
AC-16 unwanted: If discovery finds multiple supported manifests, then the reader shall diagnose ambiguity and shall not choose implicitly.
AC-17 event-driven: When a single file is converted to a document tree and back without version change, the result shall be semantically equal.
AC-18 event-driven: When a JSON document tree is converted to YAML and back, the result shall be semantically equal.
AC-19 ubiquitous: Each transform shall declare event, definition, module, or distribution retention.
AC-20 state-driven: While all transforms are event-local, definition-local, or module-local, the pipeline shall retain no more than the largest declared scope plus bounded codec buffers.
AC-21 unwanted: If a transform needs a whole distribution, then the pipeline shall report that requirement before processing.
AC-22 event-driven: When LCR v3 is migrated to v4 YAML as a file or tree, the pipeline shall use its streaming path without retaining the complete distribution.
AC-23 ubiquitous: The pipeline shall carry semantic IR events rather than JSON or YAML value trees.
AC-24 ubiquitous: Public codec options shall keep IR version, layout, format, vocabulary, normalization, and publication independent.
AC-25 event-driven: When a new codec is registered, existing migration transforms and codec callers shall compile unchanged.
AC-26 optional: Where YAML style selection is later exposed, the system shall use existing codec options without changing the semantic model.
AC-27 unwanted: If any pipeline or publication stage fails, then existing output shall remain unchanged.
AC-28 optional: Where --allow-partial is enabled, migration shall recover only through target-version incompleteness constructs.
AC-29 unwanted: If serialization would drop, coerce, or ambiguously reinterpret IR, then --allow-partial shall not permit publication.
AC-30 ubiquitous: Each diagnostic shall include stable code, stage, severity, cursor, guidance, and source location when available.
AC-31 ubiquitous: The v4 specification shall separate the semantic model, JSON profile, YAML profile, and document-tree layout.
AC-32 ubiquitous: The v4 specification shall define logical document identities without physical serialization extensions.
AC-33 event-driven: When a normative YAML example round-trips through normalized IR and JSON, the result shall be semantically equal.
notes:
Design approved and written locally at .dev/docs/superpowers/specs/2026-08-28-native-yaml-ir-storage-design.md. Native YAML and JSON normalize to versioned semantic IR. Semantic equivalence defines losslessness. Canonical YAML uses deterministic readable shorthand with explicit structural fallback. Current CLI phase adds --input-format and --output-format for JSON/YAML; YAML style selection remains a compatible follow-up. Output resolution is explicit flag, known extension, then YAML default. Input uses explicit flag, known extension, then bounded JSON-first detection. Preserve the legacy context-dependent --json behavior. Homogeneous document trees default to YAML and use manifest.yaml, module.yaml, *.type.yaml, and *.value.yaml. Approved pipeline uses semantic cursor events, composable transforms, declared event/definition/module/distribution buffering, format encoders, layout sinks, and atomic publication. Open codec identifiers leave room for TOML, Markdown, Jupyter, and other adapters without implementing them now. Approved strict diagnostics keep --allow-partial from weakening serialization correctness. Approved v4 spec split: serialization-neutral semantic model, JSON profile, YAML profile, and document-tree profile. JSON Schema remains a bootstrap definition for JSON, not a persistence restriction. Logical identities omit physical extensions; resolve format versus manifest in favor of manifest. V3 semantics remain stable with complete explicit YAML coverage; v4 schema changes are allowed with documented migration behavior. Verification uses TDD, local quality gates, real morphir-elm and morphir-scala fixtures, semantic round-trips, single-file and document-tree acceptance paths, and instrumented bounded-scope LCR streaming. Implementation will use small commits pushed at completed sectional boundaries.

## PREREQUISITE: Gherkin Acceptance Tests Required

**BEFORE IMPLEMENTATION**: Prepare comprehensive Gherkin acceptance tests and present to user for approval/iteration. Implementation may NOT proceed without user verification of tests.

- **WASM**: Compiled to WASM for extension architecture validation

The migrate extension transforms Morphir IR between v3/classic and v4 formats.

description:
Design and implement a complete Morphir daemon and extension system, enabling long-running services, IDE integration, and pluggable language/backend support.

## Vision

Create a daemon-based architecture that:
1. Provides fast, incremental compilation through persistent state
2. Enables IDE extensions (VS Code, IntelliJ, etc.) via LSP
3. Supports pluggable frontends (language bindings) and backends (code generators)
4. Offers real-time validation and type checking

---

## Phase 1: MVP Daemon (P1)

- Basic daemon process that stays running
- Unix socket or TCP communication
- Simple request/response protocol (JSON-RPC or custom)
- File watching for automatic recompilation

### Deliverables

```
┌─────────────┐     ┌─────────────────┐
│  CLI/IDE    │────▶│  Morphir Daemon │
└─────────────┘     │  ┌───────────┐  │
                    │  │  Compiler │  │
                    │  └───────────┘  │
                    │  ┌───────────┐  │
                    │  │  Cache    │  │
                    │  └───────────┘  │
                    └─────────────────┘
```

---

## Phase 2: Extension System Design (P1)

### Goals
- Define extension API and plugin interface
- Support dynamic loading of language bindings
- Support dynamic loading of code generators
- Configuration-driven extension discovery

### Extension Types
1. **Frontend Extensions** (Language Bindings)
   - Parse source language → Morphir IR
   - Examples: Gleam, Python, TypeScript, Elm

2. **Backend Extensions** (Code Generators)
   - Morphir IR → Target language/platform
   - Examples: Spark, Flink, SQL, JavaScript

3. **Analyzer Extensions**
   - Custom validation rules
   - Type inference plugins
   - Documentation generators

### Plugin Interface
```rust
pub trait FrontendExtension {
    fn name(&self) -> &str;
    fn file_extensions(&self) -> &[&str];
    fn parse(&self, source: &str) -> Result<ModuleIR>;
}

pub trait BackendExtension {
    fn name(&self) -> &str;
    fn generate(&self, ir: &Distribution) -> Result<GeneratedOutput>;
}
```

---

## Phase 3: LSP Implementation (P2)

### Goals
- Language Server Protocol implementation
- Real-time diagnostics and error reporting
- Go-to-definition, find references
- Hover information with type details
- Code completion suggestions

### Deliverables

1. Start with MVP daemon (file watch + compile)
2. Add extension loading mechanism
3. Implement LSP basics (diagnostics)
4. Expand LSP features iteratively
5. Build IDE extensions on stable LSP

### Technology Choices
- **IPC**: Unix sockets (local), TCP (remote)
- **Protocol**: JSON-RPC 2.0 (LSP compatible)
- **Plugin Loading**: Dynamic libraries or WASM

- Core Wasm boundary constraints (i32/i64/f32/f64, linear memory)
- Canonical ABI: lifting and lowering
- Scalars (bool/int/float)
- Strings and byte sequences (ptr/len, encoding)
- Lists, records/structs, tuples
- Variants/enums, option/result
- Functions, multi-arg/multi-return, flattening rules
- Resources/handles (ownership, borrowing patterns)
- Error handling and traps vs typed errors
- Versioning and evolution patterns
- Performance considerations (copies, allocations, alignment)

- Conceptual explanation with ASCII diagrams
- Code snippets in F#, Scala, Go
- Morphir IR examples (types + functions)
- Core Wasm function signature and memory layout
- WIT replacement check (what Morphir has, what's missing, candidate enhancements)
- Confidence check questions

## Key Questions
- Can Morphir IR act as an IDL/interface definition layer analogous to WIT?
- Can we derive canonical ABI lowering/lifting rules from Morphir IR types?
- What semantics does WIT have that Morphir IR lacks?
- What additions would make Morphir IR more suitable?

title: Create reusable TUI framework for interactive morphir commands
description:
Build a shared TUI framework that provides consistent interactive experiences across morphir commands.

## Overview
Create a reusable TUI component in `cmd/morphir/internal/tui` that can be used by:
- `morphir` (main interactive mode)
- `morphir validate --tui`
- Future commands like `morphir explore`, `morphir inspect`, etc.

## Architecture
```
cmd/morphir/internal/tui/
├── app.go           # Main TUI application shell
├── layout.go        # Flexible layout manager (sidebar + main)
├── components/
│   ├── sidebar.go   # Collapsible sidebar with tree/list
│   ├── viewer.go    # Markdown/content viewer with paging
│   ├── statusbar.go # Bottom status/help bar
│   └── searchbar.go # Search/filter input
├── styles/
│   └── theme.go     # Consistent lipgloss styling
└── keymap/
    └── vim.go       # Vim-style keybindings
```

## Core Components

### AppShell
Main application container that manages:
- Layout (sidebar width, visibility)
- Focus management between panels
- Global keybindings (quit, help, toggle sidebar)
- Resize handling

### SidebarPanel
- Tree view for hierarchical content
- List view for flat content  
- Collapsible (toggle with `b` or `Ctrl+b`)
- Filterable

### ViewerPanel
- Glamour-rendered markdown
- Viewport with vim navigation (j/k, gg/G, Ctrl+d/u)
- Search within content (/)
- Line numbers (optional)

### StatusBar
- Current mode indicator
- Keybinding hints
- File/position info

## Usage Pattern
```go
// In validate command
app := tui.NewApp(
    tui.WithSidebar(fileList),
    tui.WithViewer(markdownContent),
    tui.WithTitle("Validation Report"),
)
return app.Run()

// In main morphir command
app := tui.NewApp(
    tui.WithSidebar(commandList),
    tui.WithViewer(welcomeContent),
    tui.WithTitle("Morphir"),
)
return app.Run()
```

## Keybindings (Vim-style)
| Key | Action |
|-----|--------|
| j/k | Scroll down/up |
| h/l | Switch panels |
| gg/G | Go to top/bottom |
| Ctrl+d/u | Page down/up |
| / | Search |
| n/N | Next/prev search result |
| b | Toggle sidebar |
| q | Quit |
| ? | Show help |

## Libraries
- `github.com/charmbracelet/bubbletea` - TUI framework
- `github.com/charmbracelet/bubbles` - Components
- `github.com/charmbracelet/glamour` - Markdown
- `github.com/charmbracelet/lipgloss` - Styling

## Blocked By
None - this is a foundational component

## Blocks
- morphir-tol (TUI validate command)

- commit-msg, which strips Co-Authored-By trailers naming AI assistants. This is the EasyCLA compliance guard that CLAUDE.md calls critical, and it is currently unenforced - compliance depends entirely on the author remembering.
- pre-commit, which blocks committing .beads as a symlink from a worktree.
- pre-push, which runs fmt-check, lint and test.

Enabling them is not a clean 'npm install': the pre-push hook checks Go formatting ('Checking Go formatting...' then 'mise run fmt-check'), which looks like leftover text from the morphir-go template. Turning hooks on would start gating every push on tasks that may not be right for this repo, so the pre-push body should be reviewed before activation.

Suggested order: correct pre-push for this repository, then activate hooks, then confirm the commit-msg guard actually strips a test trailer.
close_reason: Activated the hooks and corrected pre-push. Root cause was that activation depended on husky's npm prepare script, which never runs in a cargo/bun/mise repository, so core.hooksPath stayed unset in every clone. Added tools/install-git-hooks.ts to set core.hooksPath to .husky without needing node, exposed as mise run hooks:install and hooks:check, and made mise run init depend on it so a normal setup activates hooks. Wired it as a dependency rather than into the init body so it also runs on Windows without POSIX bash. Found and fixed a second reason the hooks would not have run even once activated: all three were mode 100644 in the index, and git silently skips non-executable hooks on Linux and macOS; they are now 100755. Rewrote pre-push, which claimed to check Go formatting and ran cargo clippy --all-targets plus cargo test --workspace, taking many minutes and not linking on some machines; it now runs mise run fmt-check only, measured at 1.6s, with a MORPHIR_SKIP_HOOKS=1 escape hatch, on the reasoning that CI already gates lint and tests and a hook slow enough to be bypassed protects nothing. Verified the EasyCLA guard end to end by committing a message carrying a Co-Authored-By Claude trailer and confirming the stored message came back without it.

title: beads: DB and git-tracked export drift because jsonl edits bypass Dolt
description:
Reconciled on 2026-08-30: the Dolt DB and .beads/issues.jsonl had drifted in both directions - 17 issues existed only in the DB, morphir-0ley existed only in the jsonl, and 5 issues disagreed on status.

Root cause, two independent mechanisms:

1. Commit 7a211a47 (PR #739) wrote beads changes into .beads/issues.jsonl and committed them to git without a corresponding 'bd dolt push'. Both jsonl-only facts came from that one commit: morphir-0ley was created and morphir-l2p9.2 was closed, and the DB never learned either. AGENTS.md line 374 states the intended model - the DB is authoritative, sync travels over refs/dolt/data, and the jsonl is a passive export - so hand-editing the export is the documented anti-pattern. Nothing enforces it.

2. Issues created through bd were committed to Dolt but never re-exported into the git-tracked jsonl, leaving 17 DB-only records.

Amplifier: bd resolves .beads to the main checkout (C:/Users/damre/code/repos/github/finos/morphir/.beads) even when the cwd is a linked worktree. Work done in a worktree edits that worktree's tracked jsonl, while bd reads and writes the main checkout's copy. When the main checkout is behind origin/main (it was by 8 commits), bd's view of the export is stale.

Resolution applied: imported the two jsonl-authoritative records into the DB, then exported the DB over the tracked jsonl. Conflicts were resolved by updated_at - the DB was newer for the 4 h0pf records, the jsonl was newer for l2p9.2. Verified afterwards: 301 issues on both sides, no id present on only one side, no status or priority disagreement, no ids lost.

Prevention to decide on:
- 'bd hooks install' would chain DB and export automatically, but this clone has no active git hooks at all (see the separate finding about dormant husky hooks), so installing bd shims needs care about what else they chain to.
- A cheaper option is a drift check in the 'check' mise task: bd export to a temp file and diff ids and statuses against .beads/issues.jsonl, failing when they disagree.
- Either way the worktree and main-checkout .beads split should be documented in AGENTS.md, since it silently makes bd operate on a different file than the one being committed.

Also worth fixing: bd export orders the dependencies array non-deterministically, so re-exporting an unchanged issue produces a spurious diff. That churn hides real changes in review - 16 records showed as modified when only 5 had actually changed.
close_reason: Added a drift check and wired it into the commit path. tools/check-beads-drift.ts compares bd export against .beads/issues.jsonl by id, status and priority, deliberately ignoring the dependencies array because bd emits its entries in a non-deterministic order that produces diff churn without meaning disagreement. Exposed as mise run beads:drift-check, and the pre-commit hook runs it when .beads/issues.jsonl is staged, which is the moment the drift would be introduced. Verified against all three drift kinds by injecting each into a copy of the export: an issue only in the database, an issue only in the export, and a status disagreement, all detected, then confirmed a real commit with a drifted export is blocked while an in-sync one passes. Documented the invariant in AGENTS.md along with the worktree gotcha that bd resolves .beads to the main checkout even when the cwd is a linked worktree. The drift that prompted this was already reconciled in PR #748.

title: morphir ir migrate: --path-budget writer option for the portable profile
description: The v4 format defines pathBudget (default 4000, portable profile 200) and the spec says every manifest records the budget it was written with. But the writer cannot be told to use anything except the default: crates/morphir/src/commands/migrate.rs write_tree() builds CodecOptions::new(version, layout, format) with no budget parameter, and CodecOptions/DocumentTreeSink in ecosystem/morphir-rust carry none either. Editing pathBudget in an already-written manifest only relabels filenames chosen under the default. Needed: plumb a path budget through CodecOptions and the document-tree sink in morphir-rust (truncation via to_file_stem + fileNames map already exists), expose it as --path-budget on morphir ir migrate here, and record the value in the emitted manifest. Surfaced by Codex review on PR #747; docs/getting-started/morphir-cli.md now marks the portable profile as not yet writable by the CLI. title: morphir doctor: diagnose long path support and path budget
description:
Add a `morphir doctor` command that checks the local environment and reports what would break, starting with the long path handling that the IR v4 path budget depends on.

Checks it should make:
- git core.longpaths, which Git for Windows ships off, so a checkout fails past 260 characters even when Windows allows long paths
- the Windows LongPathsEnabled registry value under HKLM SYSTEM CurrentControlSet Control FileSystem
- whether the running process is longPathAware, since the registry setting alone does not help a process without the manifest declaration
- the effective usable path length, probed rather than inferred
- for a document tree in scope: the pathBudget recorded in its manifest against what this machine can actually open, and any path over 260 characters in a tree written under the long budget

It should offer the remediation rather than only naming the problem, and should exit non-zero when a tree in scope cannot be read on this machine.

Context: kb decision 0001 flips the default path budget to 4000 and requires pathBudget to be recorded in every manifest, precisely so a reader can report a mismatch up front instead of failing file by file. doctor is where that report belongs. Guidance currently lives in AGENTS.md and in the mise init task warning.

No doctor command exists yet; crates/morphir/src/commands/ has no such module.

title: v4 schema has diverged from the published v4 examples
description:
mise run examples:validate fails on the v4 examples. Pre-existing: both failed identically against the schema as committed before the naming branch.

RESOLVED so far:
- AccessControlled accepted only {Public:...} or {access,value}, not the flattened {access, TypeAliasDefinition} form the document tree spec documents and every example uses. Fixed by adding a branch and switching oneOf to anyOf.
- OpaqueTypeSpecification had an inner oneOf whose second branch (object with only "annotations") was a strict subset of the first, so any matching value matched both and "exactly one" never held. That rejected { "OpaqueTypeSpecification": {} }, the canonical form the definition documents and gives as its first example. Fixed by collapsing to one schema. books-and-records-example.json now validates.

REMAINING, and it is a design decision rather than a typo. complete-example.json encodes a parameterized type reference as a bare array:

  "typeExp": ["morphir/sdk:list#list", "a"]

Two parts of the specification disagree about what that means:
- morphir-ir-v4.yaml: TupleType accepts bare arrays *specifically because* ReferenceType does not. Its own comment reads "Unambiguous because ReferenceType does not accept bare arrays." Under this reading the value above is a 2-element Tuple.
- docs/spec/ir/schemas/v4/document-tree-files.md tells authors: "Array format: [\"morphir/SDK:list#list\", \"my-org/domain:types#user\"] (for parameterized types) ... the first element is the type constructor and subsequent elements are type arguments." Under this reading it is a parameterized Reference.

These are mutually exclusive and the difference changes what the IR means, not just whether it validates. Someone has to decide which reading is canonical, then align the other side and the examples. If Reference gains a bare-array form, the ambiguity with Tuple has to be resolved some other way.

complete-example.json also uses legacy tagged arrays for function types, e.g. "f": ["Function", {}, "a", "b"], which needs the same decision about whether v4 accepts them.
close_reason: Resolved by decision A: a bare array is a Tuple, a parameterized reference uses the Reference wrapper. Fixed AccessControlled flattened form, the OpaqueTypeSpecification overlapping oneOf, the spec page's array-format note, and rewrote both v4 examples (9 sites, incl. legacy Function and ad-hoc Tuple tags). examples:validate passes: 6 files, 0 errors.

title: Implement TypeScript binding using SWC parser crate
description:

## Background

SWC (Speedy Web Compiler) is a fast TypeScript/JavaScript compiler written in Rust. It provides production-quality parser and AST crates:
- `swc_ecma_parser` - ECMAScript/TypeScript parser
- `swc_ecma_ast` - ECMAScript/TypeScript AST types

## Goals

1. Create `morphir-typescript-binding` crate following the same pattern as `morphir-gleam-binding`
2. Use SWC's parser crate for parsing TypeScript source files
3. Transform SWC's TypeScript AST to Morphir IR
4. Leverage TypeScript's type annotations for rich type information
5. Enable roundtrip testing (TypeScript → IR → TypeScript)

## Benefits

- **Performance**: SWC is one of the fastest TS/JS parsers available
- **Correctness**: Battle-tested parser used by Next.js, Deno, and other major projects
- **Compatibility**: Full TypeScript syntax support including latest features
- **Maintenance**: Active development with regular releases

## Implementation Steps

1. Add swc_ecma_parser and swc_ecma_ast as dependencies
2. Create TypeScript AST to ModuleIR visitor
3. Handle TypeScript-specific constructs (interfaces, type aliases, generics)
4. Support both .ts and .tsx files
5. Add BDD acceptance tests with TypeScript fixtures
6. Support TypeScript project parsing (tsconfig.json awareness)

## TypeScript Features to Support

- Function declarations with type annotations
- Interface and type alias definitions
- Class definitions
- Module imports/exports
- Generic types
- Union and intersection types

## References

- SWC GitHub: https://github.com/swc-project/swc
- swc_ecma_parser crate: https://crates.io/crates/swc_ecma_parser
- swc_ecma_ast crate: https://crates.io/crates/swc_ecma_ast

title: Fix failing Gleam binding acceptance tests
description:
Several Gleam binding acceptance tests are failing and have been marked as @wip (work in progress):

## Failing Tests

### 1. Roundtrip Tests (roundtrip.feature)
- **order_validation** scenario - Parser fails on generated function signatures with tupled arguments
- **order_processing** scenario - Same parser issue with function signatures

### 2. CLI Integration Tests (cli.feature)
- All CLI tests - Require full CLI functionality to be implemented

### 3. Project Parsing Tests (project.feature)
- Module name lookup uses full path instead of module name (e.g., looking for 'main' but stored as 'src/main')

### 4. Workspace Tests (workspace.feature)
- Workspace parsing not yet implemented

### 5. Code Generation Tests (codegen.feature)
- Code generation steps not yet implemented

## Root Causes

1. **Roundtrip failures**: The Gleam parser generates function signatures with tupled parameters like `fn(#(a, b))` but cannot parse them back. The signature should be `fn(a, b)` or handle tupled parameters correctly.

2. **Project parsing**: Module names need to be derived from the file path relative to src/, not include the full path or 'src/' prefix.

3. **CLI/Workspace/Codegen**: These features are not yet implemented.

## Impact
Blocking full roundtrip testing for complex business logic fixtures.

title: Add CLI usage specs for workspace and compile commands
description:
## Context

The VFS protocol v4 design now includes comprehensive JSON-RPC methods for:
- Workspace management (create, open, close, projects, dependencies)
- Frontend compilation (workspace, project, module, files, fragment)
- VFS operations (read, propose, commit, subscribe)

## Format

Use **usage specs** (https://usage.jdx.dev/spec/) - KDL-based CLI specification format ("OpenAPI for CLIs").

Example structure:
```kdl
name "morphir"
bin "morphir"
version "4.0.0"
about "Morphir CLI - functional domain modeling toolchain"

cmd "workspace" help="Manage workspaces" {
    cmd "init" help="Create a new workspace" {
        arg "<path>" help="Workspace root directory"
        flag "-n --name <name>" help="Workspace name"
    }
    cmd "open" help="Open an existing workspace" {
        arg "<path>" help="Workspace root directory"
    }
    // ...
}

cmd "compile" help="Compile Morphir source to IR" {
    arg "[path]" help="Project or workspace path" default="."
    flag "-m --module <module>" help="Compile single module"
    flag "-i --incremental" help="Incremental compilation"
    flag "-w --watch" help="Watch for changes"
}
```

## Scope

Define usage specs for:

### Workspace Commands
- `morphir workspace init` - Create new workspace
- `morphir workspace open` - Open existing workspace  
- `morphir workspace close` - Close workspace
- `morphir workspace add` - Add project to workspace
- `morphir workspace remove` - Remove project
- `morphir workspace list` - List projects
- `morphir workspace build` - Build all projects
- `morphir workspace clean` - Clean artifacts
- `morphir workspace watch` - Watch for changes

### Compile Commands
- `morphir compile` - Compile project/workspace
- `morphir compile --module` - Compile single module
- `morphir compile --files` - Compile specific files
- `morphir compile --fragment` - Compile code fragment (REPL)

### Dependency Commands
- `morphir deps add` - Add dependency
- `morphir deps remove` - Remove dependency
- `morphir deps resolve` - Resolve dependencies
- `morphir deps list` - List dependencies

### Generate Commands
- `morphir generate` - Generate target code
- `morphir generate --target` - Specify target language

## Deliverables
- `morphir.usage.kdl` - Complete usage spec file
- Integration with shell completions (bash, zsh, fish)
- Man page generation
- Help text validation

title: IR JSON Serialization: Configurable emission strategies
description:
Add foundational JSON/JSONL serialization support to pkg/models/ir with configurable emission strategies.

## Background
Currently IR types use unexported fields, requiring ad-hoc serialization in CLI code. JSON serialization should be a first-class capability in the models package.

## Requirements

### Configurable Emission Strategies
Support different JSON emission modes via configurable MarshalJSON:

1. **Full Distribution** (traditional)
   - Emit entire Morphir IR as single JSON document
   - Compatible with existing morphir-elm tooling

2. **JSONL Split Emission** (streaming/batch)
   - Emit modules/types/values as separate JSON lines
   - Enables streaming processing of large IRs
   - Better for incremental/parallel processing

3. **Package Emission**
   - Emit with package context/metadata
   - Include package namespace, name, version

4. **Distribution Metadata**
   - Emit distribution info (version, etc.) as own JSON line
   - Support header/footer metadata lines in JSONL mode

### Implementation Approach
- Add MarshalJSON methods to IR types (ModuleDefinition, Type, Value, etc.)
- Create EmitOptions/EmitConfig for controlling emission strategy
- Support both pretty JSON and compact JSONL
- Maintain compatibility with Morphir IR JSON schema

### Types to Add JSON Support
- ModuleDefinition[TA, VA]
- ModuleDefinitionType[TA]
- ModuleDefinitionValue[TA, VA]
- TypeDefinition variants
- ValueDefinition
- Type variants (TypeReference, TypeRecord, etc.)
- Name, FQName, Path

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] json.Marshal(module) works without ad-hoc conversion
- [ ] Support full distribution emission

- [ ] Support metadata lines in JSONL
- [ ] Round-trip: Unmarshal matches original

title: Render markdown output with glamour for beautiful terminal display
description:
Enhance the existing markdown report output by rendering it beautifully in the terminal, similar to Charmbracelet's Glow CLI.

## Reference
- Glow CLI: https://github.com/charmbracelet/glow
- Glamour library (used by Glow): https://github.com/charmbracelet/glamour

## Current State
- `morphir validate --report markdown` outputs raw markdown text
- Users must pipe to external tools like `glow` or `bat` for nice rendering

## Desired State
- Automatically render markdown with glamour (the library Glow uses) when outputting to a terminal (TTY)
- Fall back to raw markdown when piped or redirected to a file
- Support `--no-color` flag to disable styling
- Achieve Glow-like beautiful rendering inline

## Implementation
```go
import "github.com/charmbracelet/glamour"

func renderMarkdown(content string) string {
    if \!isTerminal(os.Stdout) {
        return content // Raw markdown for pipes/files
    }
    
    renderer, _ := glamour.NewTermRenderer(
        glamour.WithAutoStyle(),
        glamour.WithWordWrap(terminalWidth()),
    )
    out, _ := renderer.Render(content)
    return out
}
```

## Features
- Auto-detect terminal vs pipe output
- Respect `NO_COLOR` environment variable
- Word wrap to terminal width
- Syntax highlighting for JSON code blocks (like Glow does)
- Styled tables, headers, and emphasis

## Example
```bash
# Beautiful Glow-like rendered output in terminal
morphir validate ./ir.json --report markdown

# Raw markdown when piped
morphir validate ./ir.json --report markdown > report.md
morphir validate ./ir.json --report markdown | less
```

## Libraries
- `github.com/charmbracelet/glamour` - Markdown rendering (same library Glow uses)
- `github.com/charmbracelet/lipgloss` - Styling
- `github.com/mattn/go-isatty` - TTY detection

title: Design workspace member configuration schema
description:
Design the TOML schema for declaring workspace members. Include:
- [workspace.members] array with glob patterns (e.g., 'packages/*', 'libs/**')

design:
# Workspace Members Configuration Schema

## Overview

This design follows patterns from Cargo and npm workspaces, adapted for Morphir's needs.

## 1. Workspace Root Configuration (morphir.toml)

```toml
[morphir]
version = "^3.0.0"

[workspace]
# Existing fields
root = ""
output_dir = ".morphir"

# NEW: Member discovery via glob patterns
members = [
    "packages/*",           # All direct subdirs of packages/
    "libs/**",              # Recursive: all subdirs under libs/
    "apps/*/frontend",      # Nested pattern
]

# NEW: Exclude specific paths from member discovery
exclude = [
    "packages/deprecated",
    "**/testdata",
]

# NEW: Default member to use when none specified (optional)
default_member = "packages/core"

# NEW: Shared configuration inherited by all members
[workspace.defaults]
source_directory = "src"
```

## 2. Project Section (for member projects)

Member projects use a `[project]` section in their morphir.toml:

```toml
# packages/core/morphir.toml

[project]
# Required: Project name - flexible format
# Can be any valid identifier: "my-project", "MyProject", "Morphir.Core"
name = "morphir-core"

# Optional: Package version (can inherit from workspace)
version = "1.0.0"

# Required: Directory containing source files (relative to project root)
source_directory = "src"

# Required: Modules exposed in the public API
exposed_modules = [
    "Types",
    "SDK",
    "IR",
]

# Optional: Module prefix for Elm-style qualified names
# If not set, derived from name or inferred from source structure
# Use this for morphir-elm compatibility or explicit module namespacing
module_prefix = "Morphir.Core"

# Optional: Dependencies on other workspace members
# dependencies = ["morphir-sdk"]
```

### Field Descriptions

| Field | Type | Required | Description |
|-------|------|----------|-------------|
| `name` | string | Yes | Project identifier (flexible: kebab-case, PascalCase, dot-separated, etc.) |
| `version` | string | No | Semantic version, can use `workspace = true` to inherit |
| `source_directory` | string | Yes | Source code location relative to project root |
| `exposed_modules` | []string | Yes | Public modules (without module_prefix) |
| `module_prefix` | string | No | Elm-style module prefix for qualified names (defaults to name if valid, otherwise derived) |

### Name vs Module Prefix

- **name**: Project identifier used for references, dependencies, and tooling. Flexible format.
- **module_prefix**: Elm-style dotted prefix for module qualification. Used when generating IR or for morphir-elm compatibility.

Examples:
```toml
# Modern style - explicit separation
name = "my-awesome-lib"
module_prefix = "MyAwesome.Lib"

# Elm-compatible style - name doubles as prefix
name = "Morphir.SDK"
# module_prefix defaults to "Morphir.SDK" (valid Elm module name)

# Simple project - auto-derived prefix
name = "utils"
# module_prefix defaults to "Utils" (PascalCase conversion)
```

## 3. morphir.json Compatibility (finos/morphir-elm)

The classic morphir.json format is automatically detected and mapped:

```json
{
    "name": "My.Package",
    "sourceDirectory": "src",
    "exposedModules": ["Foo", "Bar"]
}
```

### Mapping to [project] Section

| morphir.json | morphir.toml [project] |
|--------------|------------------------|
| `name` | `name` AND `module_prefix` (same value, since morphir.json names are always Elm-style) |
| `sourceDirectory` | `source_directory` |
| `exposedModules` | `exposed_modules` |

### Detection Priority

1. `morphir.toml` (preferred)
2. `.morphir/morphir.toml`  
3. `morphir.json` (legacy compatibility)

## 4. Workspace Types

### Virtual Workspace (no root project)

```toml
# Root morphir.toml - workspace only, no project
[workspace]
members = ["packages/*"]
```

### Root Package Workspace (workspace + project)

```toml
# Root morphir.toml - both workspace and project
[workspace]
members = ["libs/*"]

[project]
name = "my-app"
module_prefix = "MyApp"
source_directory = "src"
exposed_modules = ["Main"]
```

## 5. Directory Structure Examples

### Multi-package Workspace

```
my-workspace/
├── morphir.toml              # [workspace] with members
├── packages/
│   ├── core/
│   │   ├── morphir.toml      # [project] section
│   │   └── src/
│   ├── sdk/
│   │   ├── morphir.toml
│   │   └── src/
│   └── deprecated/           # Excluded
│       └── morphir.toml
└── libs/
    └── utils/
        ├── morphir.json      # Legacy format supported
        └── src/
```

### Hybrid with Root Project

```
my-app/
├── morphir.toml              # [workspace] + [project]
├── src/                      # Root project sources
└── libs/
    ├── internal/
    │   └── morphir.toml
    └── shared/
        └── morphir.json
```

## 6. Glob Pattern Specification

Patterns follow Go's `filepath.Match` plus `**` for recursive matching:

| Pattern | Matches |
|---------|---------|
| `*` | Any single path segment |
| `**` | Zero or more path segments (recursive) |
| `?` | Any single character |
| `[abc]` | Character class |

Examples:
- `packages/*` → `packages/foo`, `packages/bar` (not `packages/foo/bar`)
- `libs/**` → `libs/a`, `libs/a/b`, `libs/a/b/c`
- `apps/*/frontend` → `apps/web/frontend`, `apps/mobile/frontend`

## 7. Module Prefix Derivation

When `module_prefix` is not explicitly set:

1. If `name` is a valid Elm module name (PascalCase, dot-separated), use it directly
2. Otherwise, convert `name` to PascalCase:
   - `my-project` → `MyProject`
   - `foo_bar` → `FooBar`
   - `utils` → `Utils`

This ensures backward compatibility with morphir-elm while allowing modern naming conventions.

## 8. Config Resolution

When loading a workspace:

1. Find workspace root (walk up looking for morphir.toml with [workspace])
2. Resolve member globs against workspace root
3. Apply exclude patterns
4. For each matched directory:
   a. Look for morphir.toml with [project]
   b. Fall back to .morphir/morphir.toml
   c. Fall back to morphir.json
5. Derive module_prefix if not set
6. Merge workspace.defaults into each project
7. Return Workspace with resolved []Project

title: mise tasks using a bash shebang fail on Windows without POSIX bash
description:
Several mise tasks embed `#!/usr/bin/env bash` in their run body. On a Windows machine carrying only the WSL launcher and no POSIX bash, mise reports `no real POSIX bash found on PATH` and the task fails with a mangled temp path, exit 127.

Confirmed for `mise run init` by inspection and for the former `schema:validate`, which failed this way in practice. schema:validate has since been rewritten as a Bun and TypeScript task (tools/validate-schemas.ts) and works; init and the others have not been converted.

init could not be verified directly because running it performs `git submodule update --init --recursive`, which would overwrite locally modified submodule working trees.

Prefer TypeScript run by Bun over shell for these, consistent with the direction to move off Python and shell tooling.

title: kb sync push: export target does not check symlinked subdirectories
description: sync push writes to resolve(target, path) where target is a user-named export directory, normally the upstream checkout. A symlinked subdirectory there would be followed. Same class as the mirror containment bugs fixed in #108, but deliberately left alone: the export target is not the mirror, and real upstream checkouts legitimately contain symlinks, so tightening it risks refusing valid exports. Decision (Damian, 2026-08-28): not hardening this now. Revisit if push ever writes somewhere less trusted than a checkout the user named, or if we grow a case where an export target is attacker-influenced.
